title: Intent from Homebrew on Linux and macOS, with no source checkout: Linux binaries on every release
objective:
A developer installs Intent with Homebrew on Linux or macOS and has a working Intent with no checkout of Intent's source tree: the CLI, the daemon, the hooks and skills, and the pre-commit gate. Every release tag on GitHub carries Linux packages built by GitHub Actions beside the macOS assets, and the tap's formula installs the one that fits the machine. Windows is reached through WSL, which is ST0082's, built on this thread; there is no native Windows port.

Concretely:

1. A release workflow builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, and packages them with the support payload the binaries read at run time, so a download installs rather than being a bare binary.
2. The binaries run on Linux distributions older than the build host: they are linked statically against musl, and the workflow proves it by running them in a container at an old floor.
3. A `workflow_dispatch` run builds the same packages without a tag, so a tag is never the workflow's first run.
4. The Linux packages reach each tag's GitHub release with one writer per release object, so nothing in CI races the local release flow's `gh release create`.
5. The formula in `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` carries Linux entries for both architectures beside the macOS one, written by the release tooling, so `brew install` works on Linux as it does on macOS.
6. Intent installed from its Linux package works on Ubuntu as a user uses it, proven on hv's Ubuntu VM, whose coreutils are uutils and whose awk is mawk.
7. The docs carry Intent's Linux install through Homebrew.
8. `intent daemon start --at-login` and `intent daemon stop --at-login` refuse on Linux before they write anything.
context:
Opened 2026-10-12 and restructured on hv's word of 2026-10-14: Intent and Devbin both run from a Homebrew install on Linux and macOS, with no checkout of the source tree.

- macOS stands as it is, on hv's word of 2026-10-14; rhadamanth is not re-proved.

- `bin/devbin release check` holds one writer per release object; devbin is vendored here, so a change to its release steps is the Devbin project's to make.

Out of scope: a native Windows build (ST0082 reaches Windows through WSL), and apt.

The thread's history is in git and in each work package's commits.

wps.title: Linux release binaries built by GitHub Actions
wps.objective: A workflow builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, packages them with the support payload, proves the packaged `intent --version` runs at an old distribution floor, and keeps each package as a workflow artifact.
wps.body:
## As built

- `.github/workflows/linux-release.yml` builds both musl triples, packages them with the support payload and smokes each in `oraclelinux:7-slim`; satisfied from run 39854556183.
- The binaries are static against musl, so no glibc floor applies.
- `intent-support.tar.gz` serves Linux unchanged.

Nothing is open.

wps.title: Linux assets on each tag's GitHub release, one writer per release object
wps.objective: Each release tag's GitHub release carries the Linux assets beside the macOS ones, with one writer per release object: devbin's release core attaches them, and `bin/devbin release check` names no second writer.
wps.body:
## As built

- `linux-release.yml` runs on each `v*` tag and builds the Linux packages.
- `bin/devbin release attach vX.Y.Z` attaches them and writes `SHA256SUMS` over every asset the release carries; `bin/devbin release check` passes with `release.verbs: [check, attach]` declared in `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`.
- `bin/int macos publish` uploads the macOS assets and never writes the formula or the cask; `bin/int brew publish` alone writes both.
- `intent/docs/releasing.md` step 4 gives the order.

## Open

AC-02.1 stays unsatisfied until hv reads both halves at the 3.2.7 cut: (a) the release object carries the Linux assets beside the macOS assets, read after step 4's attach, and (b) `bin/devbin release check` names no second writer of the release object.

wps.title: Intent's Linux install through Homebrew, in docs/install.md
wps.objective: `docs/install.md` carries Intent's Linux install in a bare `## Linux` section, so its anchor is `#linux`: Homebrew on Linux, then `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent`, `intent bootstrap` and `intent doctor`, with no checkout of Intent's source tree. It is the install step's one home: ST0082's WSL page links to it and never restates it, and devbin's README points at it. The page's sections on verifying an install and on what an install has to contain read true for the Linux package, by a line or by a pointer. Every command on the page is run on Linux before it is written down: drafted from hv's Ubuntu VM, and run again from the tap once a release carries the Linux packages. Whether devbin also installs Intent is the Devbin project's call; this install is needed either way. The WSL page this package also held moved to ST0082 on 2026-10-14. Its bank also carries this thread's two lines in the release's CHANGELOG section, one for the Linux packages and the Homebrew install on Linux and one for WP-05's `--at-login` refusal (vc under hv's pen, 2026-10-13, carried here 2026-10-14).

wps.title: intent daemon start --at-login refuses on Linux before writing anything
wps.objective: On a machine without launchd, `intent daemon start --at-login` refuses before it writes anything, so no `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` plist appears on Linux, and its remedy names `intent daemon start` without the flag as the way to run the daemon. `intent daemon stop --at-login` refuses the same way. Today `daemon_start` in `intent-cli/src/render.rs` writes the plist through `launchagent::write_plist` and only then fails at `launchctl`, whose `NoLaunchctl` remedy in `intentsvcs/src/launchagent.rs` already says the right thing; the refusal moves ahead of the write. Linux CI runs the test that proves it.

wps.title: The Homebrew formula installs Intent on Linux
wps.objective: The formula the release tooling writes for `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` carries x86_64 and aarch64 Linux entries beside the macOS one, so `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent` works on Linux with no source checkout.
wps.body:
## As built

- The tap's formula keeps macOS arm64 under `on_macos` and points `on_linux`'s `on_intel` and `on_arm` at the release's musl packages; `depends_on :macos` is gone.
- AC-06.1 is satisfied from kovacs: `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent` from the published tap installed v3.2.5's aarch64 package.

## Open

A macOS re-proof on a Mac with no checkout is hv's loop-back, carried in `intent/wip.md`'s TODO; no criterion carries it.

wps.title: Intent on Ubuntu from its Linux package, as a user uses it
wps.objective: Intent installed from its Linux package, with no source checkout, works on Ubuntu as a user uses it, proven on hv's Ubuntu VM with its uutils coreutils and mawk.
wps.body:
## As built

- A package drive on kovacs passed every step: version and bootstrap, init and doctor, the thread, work package and acceptance verbs, the whiteboard, the daemon and its `--at-login` refusal, `claude upgrade --apply` with its hooks, and the critic gate.
- AC-07.1 is satisfied from that drive and hv's Claude Code session on kovacs.

Nothing is open.

criteria.text: A `workflow_dispatch` run, with no tag, builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux packaged with the support payload, and keeps each package as a workflow artifact.

Conclusion success, 21:06:43Z to 21:11:33Z: job package (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, ubuntu-latest), id 120089246768, and job package (aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, ubuntu-24.04-arm), id 120089247186, each green through bin/int linux doctor, build, package, smoke on the runner and smoke on the floor. Each package is kept as a workflow artifact: intent-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl (artifact 12459447395, 14576654 bytes, digest sha256:9c386af2b961) and intent-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl (artifact 12459690768, 13589688 bytes, digest sha256:e63d2e01e4cc), both kept until 2027-01-20. Downloaded and listed by cc, never run: each tarball (x86_64 sha256 9e9ae9f6b7f9, aarch64 ed579ded2241) holds bin/intent and bin/intentd, statically linked (x86-64 static-pie; ARM aarch64 static), beside the support payload the binaries read at run time, intent/plugins and lib/templates, whose 180 files are byte-identical, exec bits included, in both packages and in v3.2.5's intent-support.tar.gz (sha256 d0938ba5832f); the tarball's only extra is three empty directories git does not track (lib/templates/eng, issues and prime). The run's records, both floor steps and these listings are refs/bank/cc/0081/evidence/run-39854556183.txt (blob baec68a54b14).

criteria.text: The same run executes the packaged `intent --version` inside a container of the oldest Linux distribution the workflow names as its floor, and that step fails the run when the binary does not start.

state.evidence: The same run, 39854556183 (hv's --ref main workflow_dispatch of 2026-10-22, conclusion success). In both jobs (ids 120089246768 and 120089247186) the step `smoke, on the floor (AC-01.2)` ran `bin/int linux smoke --in "$FLOOR"` with FLOOR oraclelinux:7-slim, the one floor the workflow names (Oracle Linux 7, glibc 2.17), pulled at digest sha256:1add6ed8602e. Inside that container the packaged binary, reached through a link on PATH, printed `intent 3.2.5 (2e0e9215d67f67c665d1b8179a7888555551c8e7) dev` on each leg, then resolved its install root to /opt/intent-<triple> and ran the support tree's gate hook both ways. The step fails the run when the binary does not start, by reading: bin/.devbin/cmd/linux runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 20) and pipes smoke_checks into the container's `/bin/bash -euo pipefail -s`, whose first check is `intent --version`, so a binary that does not start ends the container's shell non-zero, which ends `bin/int` non-zero, which fails the step (its shell, as the log shows, is `/usr/bin/bash -e {0}`), the job and the run; that clause was read, not driven with a broken binary. Both floor steps are quoted in refs/bank/cc/0081/evidence/run-39854556183.txt (blob baec68a54b14).
